title: Special Social Problems; Statistical Approaches to Examining Race, Ethnicity, and Racism
description: This course will examine major statistical approaches to measure race, ethnicity, and racism. It will focus on ways to test theories related tosystemic racism, prejudice, discrimination, intersectionality, colorism, critical race theory, and public health critical race praxis. The course will provide students with tools to measure race and ethnicity ona micro-, meso-, and macro-level. Students will be exposed to a myriadof data sets and statistical packages for engaging in categorical data analysis, factor analysis, and Likert scaling when assessing race, ethnicity, and racism. Students will also be exposed to innovative and cutting-edge approaches (such as virtual reality) relatedto collecting data on racism. Students should already have statistical training in regression,have taken an introduction to statistics course at the graduate level, and be competent using Stata.
